title: Watch the light hit El Capitan in Yosemite Valley
description: Granite walls a kilometre high above a glacial valley. US national parks restrict dogs to paved areas and campgrounds only.

title: Hike below the rim of the Grand Canyon
description: Going down is optional, coming back up is not - rangers pull people off the Bright Angel Trail every summer. Go in spring or autumn.

title: Watch the Grand Prismatic Spring from the overlook
description: The world's first national park, sitting on an active supervolcano. The overlook trail beats the boardwalk for seeing the colours.

title: Wade The Narrows in Zion
description: Walking up the Virgin River between 300m walls that close to nine metres apart. Closed whenever flash flood risk is high - check daily.

title: Watch sunrise through Mesa Arch at Canyonlands
description: For about twenty minutes at dawn the underside of the arch glows orange from light bouncing off the canyon below.

title: See the first sunrise in the US from Cadillac Mountain
description: From October to March this is the first place in the continental US to catch the sun. Acadia is unusually dog-friendly for a national park.

title: Follow the brass bands down Frenchmen Street
description: Where locals go when tourists go to Bourbon Street - live jazz in a dozen rooms within three blocks, most nights of the year.

title: Drive the surviving stretches of Route 66
description: Decommissioned in 1985 and replaced by interstates, but long segments survive as business routes through towns the freeway bypassed.

title: Stand under the tallest trees on earth in Redwood
description: Coast redwoods reach over 110m. The tallest known tree's location is deliberately unpublished to protect the ground around its roots.

title: Drive Highway 1 through Big Sur
description: 140km of coast road on the edge of the Santa Lucia range. Landslides close sections for months at a time - check before committing.

title: Take the bus into Denali
description: One 148km road into six million acres, and private vehicles are barred beyond mile 15. Grizzly, caribou, moose and wolf all along it.

title: Watch Kilauea glow after dark
description: One of the most active volcanoes on earth. Whether there is anything to see depends entirely on the current eruption - check the USGS status first.

title: Drive the Going-to-the-Sun Road in Glacier
description: 80km over Logan Pass, only fully open for about ten weeks a year, and now requiring a timed entry reservation in peak season.

title: Sled the gypsum dunes at White Sands
description: 275 square miles of white gypsum sand you can toboggan down. Dogs are allowed on leash almost everywhere here, unusually.

title: Walk the Notch Trail in Badlands
description: A wooden ladder up a cliff face leads to a ledge over the White River valley, through eroded sediment laid down 75 million years ago.

title: Walk the Hoh Rain Forest in Olympic
description: A temperate rainforest getting up to 4 metres of rain a year, with moss hanging off every branch - and glaciers and coast in the same park.

title: Paddle the mangroves in the Everglades
description: A river 100km wide and 15cm deep, and the only place where alligators and crocodiles share territory. Go in the dry season for the wildlife.

title: Walk the High Line end to end
description: A disused elevated freight line turned 2.3km linear park through Manhattan's west side. Free, and dogs are not permitted.

title: Canoe on Moraine Lake in Banff
description: Rock flour suspended in glacial meltwater gives that colour. Private vehicles are now banned on the Moraine Lake road - shuttle only.

title: Drive the Icefields Parkway to Jasper
description: 232km past more than 100 glaciers between Lake Louise and Jasper - routinely called one of the great drives anywhere.

title: Stargaze in Jasper's Dark Sky Preserve
description: One of the largest accessible dark sky preserves in the world, with a decent chance of aurora on clear winter nights.

title: Walk the sea floor at Hopewell Rocks
description: The highest tides on earth, up to 16m. You walk on the ocean floor at low tide and kayak over the same spot six hours later.

title: Drive the Cabot Trail in autumn
description: 298km around Cape Breton's highlands, through Acadian and Gaelic communities, at its best when the maples turn in early October.

title: See polar bears at Churchill
description: Bears gather here waiting for Hudson Bay to freeze. There is no road in - you arrive by train or plane, and go out in a tundra buggy.

title: Visit the Watchmen sites on Haida Gwaii
description: Standing mortuary poles at SGang Gwaay, guarded by Haida Watchmen and deliberately left to return to the earth. Access is permitted and limited.

title: Take the boat under Horseshoe Falls
description: Around 2,800 cubic metres a second go over the Horseshoe. The Canadian side has the view; the boat gets you into the spray.

title: Walk the walled old town of Quebec City
description: The only walled city north of Mexico, founded 1608, and the most convincingly European place in North America.

title: Drive the Dempster Highway to the Arctic Ocean
description: Around 900km of gravel from Dawson City to Tuktoyaktuk on the Arctic Ocean. Carry two spare tyres - this is not an exaggeration.

title: Swim in a cenote near Valladolid
description: Thousands of limestone sinkholes over a flooded cave system, sacred to the Maya and the peninsula's only natural fresh water.

title: Hear the Kukulkan pyramid echo at Chichen Itza
description: Clap at the base of El Castillo and the staircase returns a chirp said to imitate the quetzal. Twice a year a serpent shadow runs down the steps.

title: Ride El Chepe through Copper Canyon
description: A canyon system deeper and four times larger than the Grand Canyon, crossed by a railway with 37 bridges and 86 tunnels.

title: Eat your way through the Oaxaca markets
description: Seven moles, tlayudas, mezcal and chapulines - widely held to be the best regional cooking in Mexico, and it is not close.

title: Meet grey whales in San Ignacio Lagoon
description: Grey whales calve here and mothers routinely push their calves up to the boats to be touched - one of the strangest wildlife encounters anywhere.

title: Stand in the monarch butterfly forests of Michoacan
description: Hundreds of millions of monarchs arrive after a 4,000km migration and cover the oyamel firs so densely the branches bend.

title: Snorkel the reef at Akumal
description: Part of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, the second largest on earth, with green turtles grazing the seagrass close to shore.

title: See the Milky Way from Great Basin National Park
description: Some of the darkest skies left in the continental US, plus bristlecone pines that were already thousands of years old when Rome fell.

title: Look into Crater Lake
description: The deepest lake in the US at 594m, filling a caldera left when Mount Mazama collapsed about 7,700 years ago. Fed only by rain and snow.

title: Watch the synchronous fireflies in the Smokies
description: For about two weeks each June, one firefly species here flashes in unison. Access is by lottery, and it is worth entering.
